C45039.observed: What was checked: which money boxes you are allowed to type over, for the three kinds of part the case names. What happened, in all three cases as the case requires. (1) A catalogue part - its card in the search list says "Catalog" rather than showing a stock quantity - opens with its cost and sell price filled in from the catalogue and BOTH accept being typed over; 13.13 and 26.26 were entered and stayed. (2) A stocked part - its card shows "Inventory Qty" and a bin - opens with its cost locked, so the cost really does come from the stock record and cannot be edited on the work order, while the sell price still accepts a new figure (77.77 was entered and stayed). (3) Setting the part's Source to "Found" through "More options" locks the vendor, the cost, the core charge and the margin: before the change all four were empty and could be typed in, and after it none of them accepts a keystroke.
C45039.not_observed: On the Found part the case says those fields are 'empty'; they are fixed and read-only as required, but cost and core charge display 0.00 and margin displays 100 rather than being blank. Flagged for review - it is what is shown, not what the part is worth.

C45001.observed: What was checked: whether the description that arrives with a chosen part can be typed over, and whether that differs between a catalogue part and a stocked one. What happened: for a catalogue part - the search card says "Catalog" - the description arrives filled in and accepts being overwritten; this was tried on four different catalogue parts and each one took the new wording. For a stocked part - the card shows "Inventory Qty" and a bin - the description is locked and cannot be changed at all; this was tried on five different stocked parts and every one refused. That is the difference the case describes: a part that belongs to the stock record keeps the stock record's wording, while a part being requested from the catalogue can be described however the shop needs.
C45001.not_observed: Whether description, cost, core charge and vendor become read-only after the part request is saved was still being checked when this result was written; it is recorded separately.

C45253.observed: What was checked: whether changing the part's Category changes the sell price, since different categories are priced with different mark-ups. What happened: with the cost held at 40.00 and nothing else touched, the sell price moved every time the category changed - Uncategorized gave 100.00, 70%override gave 68.00, AUTO-Batteries gave 80.00, and AUTO-Accessories and AUTO-Body each gave 100.00. So the pricing rules for the chosen category are applied straight away, which is what this case asks for. IMPORTANT - please read: this case carries a note saying the sell price does NOT move when the category changes and stays at 86.32 throughout. That is no longer what the build does. Under the case's own third outcome this is the good one: the behaviour now works, so the note should be removed from the case.
